what_happened: Live reproduction of the dispatch's naive basename-grep orphan check found the false-positive set has grown from 16 (present-extension talk/contents templates) to 39, with a second extension (founder's deck/contents templates, 23 files) now exhibiting the identical directory-reference pattern. Corrected the regression fixture floor from 16 to 39 in the research report before Phase 1 probe design proceeds.

The research report pre-answered three questions the plan would otherwise have had to re-derive: the corrected 39-file regression floor (vs the dispatch's stale 16), the absence of a merged index.json in the source store (22 per-extension index-entries.json files instead), and a definitive negative verdict on context-file-granularity telemetry. Planning needed no re-derivation and no second research round.

Research recommended naming the probe scripts/context-inventory.sh, but the task's declared file_scope names scripts/context-reachability.sh (and tests/test-context-reachability.sh). Plan follows the declared file_scope names to avoid a cosmetic file-scope excursion; divergence recorded in the plan's Research Integration section.

The dispatch requires Phase 3's removal/merge targets to be named individually and added to file_scope AT PLAN TIME, but those targets are only knowable after the probe RUNS at implement time. Resolved by making the live-run phase a decision gate: the expected-empty confirmed-dead set closes with Reasoned Exclusions citing the probe verdict, and a non-empty set STOPS and reports rather than editing undeclared paths.

verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4 reported 7 FAIL issues from check-extension-docs.sh (deployed-script content drift on git-commit-scoped.sh/lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh/test-git-commit-scoped.sh/test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, plus Rule R line_count mismatches on formats/return-metadata-file.md and standards/git-staging-scope.md). All 7 are attributable to sibling task 304's concurrent, uncommitted/in-flight source-store edits (confirmed against its declared file_scope), not to this task's own edits. This task's own new files (context-reachability.sh, its test) were correctly reported as 'script not deployed, skipping drift check' (informational only, not part of the 7 FAIL count).

Phase 6 decision gate: confirmed-dead set is EMPTY (0 of 591 files). Closed the removal/merge/split sub-steps via Reasoned Exclusions in ranked-disposition.md rather than performing any edit -- matches the research's own expected outcome exactly. No file_scope excursion needed.

Editing context-discovery.md (Phase 7) introduced a new Rule R line_count mismatch for its own index-entries.json entry (379 vs actual 402), caught by check-extension-docs.sh. Applied a correct, narrow one-line fix (updated only that one entry's line_count to 402) directly in core/index-entries.json. However, that file currently ALSO carries roughly a dozen OTHER uncommitted line_count repairs from unrelated, already-in-flight sibling work (including task 304's own declared git-staging-scope.md entry), none of which this task owns or should commit. Left the one-line fix applied in the working tree (confirmed it clears the gate finding) but deliberately did NOT add index-entries.json to this task's own files_touched/commit -- committing the whole file would sweep in every other uncommitted sibling hunk. This task's own phase-7 commit stages only context-discovery.md.

run-all.sh full suite: 135 passed, 3 failed (test-lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh, test-four-tier-conflict.sh). Investigated each: (1) test-lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh tests lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh, which is literally in sibling task 304's declared file_scope. (2) test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh tests verify-deploy.sh, confirmed mid-edit by the sibling (43 lines changed, uncommitted) per the dispatch's own WORKING-TREE CONDITION note; it hangs/times out when run standalone too, consistent with an in-flight, not-yet-complete sibling edit, not a regression from this task. (3) test-four-tier-conflict.sh PASSES cleanly standalone (13/13, exit 0) -- its failure inside the full run-all.sh run was a transient flake under full-suite system load, not a real regression. None of the three relate to this task's own file_scope; this task's own new suite (test-context-reachability.sh) passed within the same full run.

test-four-tier-conflict.sh's Case 6 ('budget-bound') asserts a conflict-resolution wait completes within [1000ms, 2000ms). Under this session's own heavy concurrent bash/grep/subprocess load (running the full-suite run-all.sh repeatedly plus many live-tree probe invocations), it measured elapsed_ms=2808, outside the budget, 3 separate times across repeated standalone runs. This is a load-sensitive timing assertion in a file completely unrelated to this task's scope (task-lock.md's conflict-response ladder, not context-reachability.sh), and is plausibly also responsible for test-four-tier-conflict.sh's earlier NEW-failure appearance inside the first full run-all.sh pass before this task's own load subsided. Not attributable to this task's edits; not fixed (out of file_scope).
